triage.reason: The motor stopped 13 ms after the pinch threshold was crossed, at -30 °C and 9 V. The limit is 10 ms, so the pinch is not stopped in time.
Retained power after ignition off ends at about 50 s instead of 60 s. A limit is missed without a safety effect, and turning the ignition on is a workaround.
The WLC_Status period of 97 to 104 ms is within 100 ms ± 10 ms. Information only.
False pinch reversal during express close at about -20 °C with no obstacle. Express close works wrongly in normal cold-weather use.
Typo in a comment only. The code is correct.
Same problem as DR-1001: the pinch stop is late (14 ms) at -30 °C and low supply voltage.

Sleep current is 140 µA against a 100 µA limit, probably because the CAN transceiver stays in standby instead of sleep. A limit is missed without a safety effect. The power design owns the sleep current, but the fix may be in how the transceiver is put to sleep.
False reversal caused by road vibration on cobblestones (2 in 10 tries). This is a different condition from the cold-weather false reversal in DR-1004, so it is not a duplicate.
After overcurrent, B1A02 is not stored and the fault state is not set. Fault reporting is lost. The motor does stop, so there is no safety effect.
Too vague to judge: two subjective clinic comments and no measurement. The switch-to-motor response time needs to be measured before the severity can be confirmed.
Same problem as DR-1004: false reversal during auto-up in cold weather (-18 °C) with no obstacle.
The thermal block lets one more movement through after the model passes 140 °C. The motor protection works wrongly, but no direct risk to a person is shown.
Position drifts 3.5 mm over 200 cycles. Accuracy is degraded. No limit is given; check whether the drift could shift the anti-pinch or soft-stop zones.

At 16 V the motor keeps running for 180 ms after switch release (limit 100 ms); at 13.5 V it is 60 ms. Release detection works wrongly at high supply voltage. Anti-pinch is assumed to stay active, so this is not rated S1. The voltage dependence could also point to the drive path, so the cause needs confirming.
Same problem as DR-1002: retained power after ignition off is shorter than 60 s.
Under diagnostic load, one WLC_Status frame was dropped (a 200 ms gap). A timing limit is missed rarely.
Documentation error in the draft owner's manual. This is not a controller defect; switch_input is only the closest component.
Loss of the Hall signal is not detected: no plausibility check, no DTC, and the motor runs to the end stop. Without Hall pulses anti-pinch cannot work, so a person could be hurt.
Same problem as DR-1012: one opening is allowed above the 140 °C thermal block.
Express close is available while the window is not normalized. Without a valid position, pinch protection cannot be relied on, so the safety function is bypassed.
Unused variable that only causes a compiler warning. Cosmetic.
3 of 100 diagnostic responses took 55 to 62 ms (limit 50 ms), during motor start. Rare, and a limit is missed without a safety effect.
Same problem as DR-1008: false reversal on a cobblestone road.
Reverse polarity protection fails: diode D3 opens and the controller is dead afterwards. All function is lost.
The undervoltage stop at 21 ms is within the 50 ms limit. Information only.
Loud knock when the window reaches the top seal (end-stop behaviour). Subjective, with no measurement and no damage. Degraded quality only.
Same problem as DR-1018: Hall sensor loss is not detected, the motor keeps running into the seal, and no DTC is stored.
The spec has no limit for inrush current, so this is information only: a proposal for a new requirement.
Same problem as DR-1009: after overcurrent, the fault state is not set and no DTC is stored.

Reversal distance is 146 mm at 85 °C against the v1.3 limit of 150 mm. The window does reverse, so this is rated S2 rather than S1. The safety team should confirm whether the shorter distance affects freeing a trapped person; if so, raise it to S1.
